title: Humpback Whales Rebounded To 25,000 After Near-Extinction In One Region
hook: Western South Atlantic humpbacks rebounded to about 25,000 after near-extinction.
closing: Recovery is possible, but a regional comeback does not mean every whale population is safe.
question: What makes wildlife protection succeed long term?

segments.say: The western South Atlantic estimate reaches 25,000 humpbacks. That regional rebound shows a severely depleted population can recover.
The supplied tally lists 10 recovered humpback populations. Other populations remain listed, so recovery is not universal.
Commercial whaling killed about 2.9 million large whales during the measured century. This total covers large whales, not only humpbacks.
